The most powerful refutation is the “swine objection”: if pleasures differ only in quantity, a satisfied pig’s life could outrank a dissatisfied Socrates’s, contradicting our considered judgments about higher and lower pleasures. This exposes the calculus’s failure to capture qualitative distinctions and its implausible reduction of all value to a single hedonic scale. The team note about unforeseeable consequences is a practical usability worry, but the swine objection strikes at the theory’s core evaluative standard.
